title: Tauri 2 Control Room skeleton, read-only, Windows (lean: no Vite, no Tauri CLI, no React, no Stop)
dependency_notes: CR-01 (orcel-app-api/1, the endpoint read) and CR-02 (the headless client in apps/orcel-control-room, whose reducer and validators the front end reuses) are merged backlog work with no SpecGrain spec of their own; SG-000118 was only their proposed grain. SG-000122 is the founder's sequencing gate (forms on real Edge 157), met for starting engineering by founder decision 1 of 2026-11-16. SG-000126 serves task.list and task.get, admitted as read-only metadata by founder decision 5. FD-03 is answered by the founder's Decision 4.
objective: Give Orcel a secure, lightweight, professional, read-only desktop interface on Windows, built on Tauri 2 and working with the existing daemon and MCP architecture. Lean: no Vite, no Tauri CLI, no React, configuration written from scratch, a minimal TypeScript UI, no Stop control. The Tauri Rust process is the only client of orceld's local app API (orcel-app-api/1): it opens this user's pipe as an identification-only client, confirms the server runs as this user at Medium integrity or above, and sends only status.get, capabilities.get, events.subscribe, task.list and task.get. Report tasks are shown as read-only metadata (state, safe workspace-relative paths and hashes), never content. The web view reaches that data only through five typed Tauri commands under a strict CSP with embedded assets only, and performs no browser, filesystem, shell or privileged action. orceld remains the sole security and authorization authority; the window answers no approval and changes no state. Windows only, development builds only. This is the draft of docs/orcel/implementation-readiness/prep/SG-000119.md and activates nothing by itself.

include: Activate the SG-000119 contract only (slice A0), on the founder's go-ahead on the tracking issue opened from this reviewed spec. Every slice below needs its own exact-head qualified implementation PR with a fresh-context security review, exact-head CI and the relevant native Windows tests before merge.

Slice A1, the Rust app API client: crates/orcel-app-api-client in the root workspace, using only std, windows-sys 0.52 and libc already in the root lock. Windows: open \\.\pipe\orcel-<user SID>-app with SECURITY_SQOS_PRESENT | SECURITY_IDENTIFICATION, read GetNamedPipeServerProcessId, and require the server's token user to equal this process's and its integrity to be Medium or above before the first write (lifted from orceld's describe_holder and token_user). Unix endpoint checks as code only (not qualified here). A closed method enum of status.get, capabilities.get, events.subscribe, task.list and task.get; 64 KiB frames; epoch-aware cursors with gap rejection before the cursor moves.

Slice A1, the task bound (founder decision 5): every task.list and task.get answer is re-shaped in Rust before the web view sees it. A field allowlist keeps task_id, kind, state, owner, workspace_id, created_at_ms, updated_at_ms, title (planner-supplied, capped at 120 characters, labelled), folder, sources path/sha256/bytes, proposal and report name/destination/sha256/bytes, steps step_id/kind/outcome/at_ms, and from check only checker, passed, destination, bytes, sha256, sources_unchanged, figures_confirmed and checked_at_ms; every other field is dropped. A path is shown only if workspace-relative (not empty, no drive letter, no leading separator, no UNC or \\?\ prefix, no .. or . segment, no NUL or control character, at most 1024 bytes); otherwise it is withheld. A hash is shown only as 64 lowercase hex characters. No path is ever joined to a workspace root, opened or resolved.

Slice A2, the Tauri skeleton: apps/orcel-control-room/src-tauri as its own Cargo workspace with its own Cargo.lock, deny.toml and notices, excluded from the root workspace; tauri and tauri-build pinned exactly with default-features off and only wry and custom-protocol on; tauri.conf.json and one capability file written from scratch; embedded assets, the recorded CSP, navigation and new-window refusal, drag-drop off, devtools off, refusal to start when any WEBVIEW2_* environment variable is set, an explicit WebView2 user data folder outside orceld's state root; a static not-connected page. This slice performs the download approved by founder decision 3, under its review conditions.

Slice A3, the bridge: five Tauri commands, app_status, app_capabilities, app_events (a tauri::ipc::Channel stream), app_tasks and app_task (task_id at most 128 bytes of [A-Za-z0-9_-]), over A1; permissions generated by tauri_build AppManifest for exactly these five; invoke_handler registers exactly these five.

Slice A4, the view: minimal plain HTML, CSS and TypeScript compiled by the typescript 5.9.3 already locked in apps/orcel-control-room, no bundler; status, capabilities with unavailable reasons, the device list shown unavailable (devices.list is reserved), the timeline from events using the headless client's reducer, report tasks as metadata with withheld paths shown as withheld; pending approvals shown only as waiting for approval on this device; every field rendered as text.

Slice A5, accessibility and the Windows run: keyboard-only use, screen reader names, RTL layout, 100/150/200% scaling, UI Automation checks adapted from PR #282's checks that apply to a read-only view, native evidence that the WebView2 renderer cannot open the pipe, and measurements of cold and warm start, working set and binary size beside the WPF preview for CR-04.

Slice A6 (optional, non-blocking): a macOS compile check only, cargo build --locked and the A2 and A3 Rust tests of src-tauri on a disposable macos-latest runner; the window is never launched and nothing on macOS is qualified.

Slice A7, closeout: canonical evidence, the resolved crate versions, the known limits, and an explicit statement that forms and workbooks human acceptance is not claimed and the three skipped machine-mutating browser tests stay UNVERIFIED.
exclude: Stop of any kind (deferred to a later grain by founder decision 7): task.stop, emergency revoke, Stop desktop control, or any control that changes orceld state.
approval.history, clients.list and every app API method other than the five listed; report content, source content, secrets and any location outside a workspace.
Answering, cancelling, dismissing, minting, scripting or forwarding an approval; any affordance that looks like one; any bypass of a human approval prompt.
Any browser, filesystem, shell or privileged action from the UI, directly or through a plugin; opening or revealing any path.

React, Vite, the Tauri CLI, tauri-driver, msedgedriver, @tauri-apps/api or any other npm package not already locked; the AgentKit React components and @tabler/icons-react; global installs and paid services.
Copying Cua Spaces' src-tauri scaffolding (FSL) or the cua-driver Tauri fixture's main.rs, tauri.conf.json or tiny_http server; the fixture itself is unchanged.
Any Tauri plugin (shell, fs, http, dialog, opener, process, updater, clipboard, notification, global-shortcut, deep-link, store or other).
Remote content, a devUrl, a dev server, any listener, remote IPC access, devtools in release-profile builds, additional WebView2 browser arguments, and macOSPrivateApi.
Public installers, bundles, updater artifacts, code signing, releases and deployment (founder decision 6); bundle.active stays false.
Linux entirely (no src-tauri Linux leg, no WebKitGTK package anywhere); native qualification on macOS. Both are later, independently qualified stages (founder decision 2).
Unrestricted dependency upgrades; any crate source other than crates.io and Orcel's own path crate.
Retiring the WPF preview (CR-04) or changing it.
Running or claiming the three skipped machine-mutating browser tests; claiming forms or workbooks human acceptance.

authority_delta.activation: None. This packet authorizes implementing and proving SG-000119; it adds no dependency, command, listener or authority by itself.
authority_delta.app_api: None. The Control Room is a new client of the existing orcel-app-api/1 endpoint, sending only status.get, capabilities.get, events.subscribe, task.list and task.get; no method is added to orceld and task.stop is not sent.
authority_delta.ui: Proposed only (slices A2 to A5): a read-only Tauri window whose web view can invoke exactly five commands that return validated read results, with report tasks bounded to metadata. It shows pending approvals as waiting for approval on this device and cannot answer them.
authority_delta.dependencies: Proposed only (slice A2, approved by founder decision 3 under its review conditions): the Tauri 2 crate graph from crates.io in a separate workspace with an exact-pinned lock, and the system web view (WebView2 on Windows). Slice A1 adds no dependency.
authority_delta.filesystem: None. The UI reads no file and resolves no path; task paths are displayed as text only.
authority_delta.network: None. No listener, no remote content, no connect-src beyond Tauri's IPC origin, no remote IPC.
authority_delta.process: One new unprivileged per-user desktop process and the system web view's own processes; none is spawned by orceld.
authority_delta.approval: None. Approvals stay with the OS presence surfaces and are never bypassed.
authority_delta.release: None. Development builds only; nothing enters the release payload.
authority_delta.privileged: None. SG-000096 Full User shell remains unarmed.

invariants: orceld remains the sole security and authorization authority; the Control Room reads and displays only.
The first interface is read-only: no control changes orceld state, and Stop is absent.
The UI performs no direct browser, filesystem, shell or privileged action, and no plugin provides one.
No human approval prompt is answered, scripted, suppressed or bypassed; pending approvals are displayed as waiting for approval on this device only.

The Tauri Rust process is the only app API client; on Windows it opens the pipe as an identification-only client and confirms the server's token user equals its own and its integrity is Medium or above before the first write.
Only status.get, capabilities.get, events.subscribe, task.list and task.get can be sent; the method set is a closed enum, not a string allowlist.

Task answers pass the field allowlist, the workspace-relative path rule and the hash rule in Rust before the web view; report content, secrets and locations outside a workspace never reach the UI; no path is opened or resolved.

The web view can invoke exactly app_status, app_capabilities, app_events, app_tasks and app_task; the capability file grants exactly their five permissions to the main window; no core default permission, no remote section, no plugin.

The CSP is default-src 'none'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self'; img-src 'self'; font-src 'self'; connect-src ipc: http://ipc.localhost; frame-src 'none'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'none', narrowed only by evidence; no unsafe source.

Assets are embedded; there is no devUrl, dev server or listener; navigation away from Tauri's asset origin and new windows are refused; drag-drop is off; devtools are absent from release-profile builds.
The process refuses to start when any WEBVIEW2_* environment variable is set and passes no additional browser arguments.
Every field from orceld is rendered as text; no HTML sink, eval or Function exists in the minimal TypeScript front end.

src-tauri is its own workspace with exact pins, crates.io sources only, a checked-in Cargo.lock with checksums, reviewed lock changes, cargo deny licenses and cargo audit; root builds and the release payload never include it; no unrestricted upgrade, global install or paid service.
Development builds only; bundle.active is false; no public installer, updater, signing, release or deployment without separate authorization.
Security review, exact-head CI and the relevant native Windows tests precede every merge.

The three skipped machine-mutating browser tests stay UNVERIFIED, and forms and workbooks human acceptance is never claimed until the founder's personal journeys pass; scripted approvals are never human approvals or final release qualification.
acceptance: Activation (A0): this spec, CURRENT.md's record of the founder go-ahead on the tracking issue, Decision 4 and the 2026-11-16 decisions, and the open-grain pins land together; no code or dependency changes.

Client tests (A1): against a real orceld, each allowed method answers; an unlisted method cannot be constructed; an over-cap frame is refused; a gap is rejected before the cursor moves; a new epoch clears the timeline; daemon down answers a typed unavailable; on Windows a pipe served by another account or below Medium integrity is refused before any write.

Task bound tests (A1): an unknown field is dropped; absolute, drive-letter, rooted, UNC, \\?\-prefixed, .. or . segment, control-character and over-long paths are withheld; a malformed hash is withheld; the title is capped; no output field carries file content.

Skeleton tests (A2): a Rust test asserts the exact CSP, the capability file's single window and permission list, no remote section, no devUrl and bundle inactive; the navigation predicate refuses https:, http://127.0.0.1, file:, data: and javascript: and allows only the asset origin; cargo tree shows no tauri-plugin-* and no listener crate; every lock source is crates.io; cargo deny licenses and cargo audit pass with each warning recorded; a WEBVIEW2_* variable stops startup with a stated reason; the dependency review records versions, sources, checksums, the lock diff and licenses.

Bridge tests (A3): the AppManifest command list and the invoke_handler list are equal; an unknown command invoked from the page is refused by the ACL; an extra argument and a malformed task_id are refused; the event Channel ends when the window closes.

View tests (A4): the reducer's gap, duplicate and epoch cases pass on the compiled modules; a static check finds no innerHTML, insertAdjacentHTML, document.write, eval, Function or inline handler; no element answers an approval or opens a path; control and bidi characters are replaced; a withheld path is shown as withheld.

Windows run (A5): UI Automation checks pass on windows-latest and on the founder's PC through a live orceld; keyboard-only and Narrator checks recorded; the renderer is shown unable to open the pipe; start, memory and size measured beside the WPF preview; each run records its WebView2 version.
Optional macOS compile check (A6): the A2 and A3 Rust tests pass on macos-latest; nothing on macOS is claimed.

Closeout (A7): canonical evidence, the resolved versions written into this spec and the prep packet, the known limits, and the explicit non-claims for forms and workbooks human acceptance and the three skipped machine-mutating browser tests.
